correctness.rationale: The positive endemic prey Jacobian has strictly negative diagonal entries and opposite-sign off-diagonal entries, so trace<0 and determinant>0. At the predator-free state the delayed linearization is block upper triangular and its predator factor is λ+h−p exp(−λτ). For p<h a modulus estimate excludes all nonnegative-real roots; p=h has one simple zero; p>h has a strictly positive real root for every τ. The only imaginary frequency is sqrt(p²−h²), its phase gives the full delay sequence, and implicit differentiation gives strictly positive crossing velocity. Standard retarded root counting yields the complete unstable dimension ladder; persistent positive real multiplier makes nearby Hopf orbits unstable if they occur. Globally, logistic prey domination gives limsup x≤K, which bounds per-capita delayed predator birth by q_epsilon<h; scalar delayed comparison gives exponential predator decay for every fixed finite delay. Exact symbolic/rational checker confirms the reproducible example. For any periodic orbit sufficiently close to the predator-free state with p>h, the instantaneous delayed predator recruitment factor q exceeds h uniformly. Integrating the predator equation over a full period gives 0=integral (q-h)z; this forbids any nontrivial nonnegative periodic predator abundance, while algebraic Hopf branches can only be sign-changing. Well-posedness is ensured by strictly positive susceptible- and infected-prey histories and nonnegative predator history: y'≥-(ν+n/c)y prevents simultaneous zero denominators at future times; x and y are bounded by logistic/linear comparison and z has at-most-linear delayed growth, so the necessary positive solution exists globally.

value.rationale: The model motivating theorem presents possible delay-driven Hopf behavior at the predator-free boundary but does not resolve whether predators are already able to invade or whether local periodic offspring could be stable. The exact all-delay invasion threshold, complete growing unstable-dimension ladder, and prohibition of small stable Hopf offspring close that biologically relevant stability gap. The independent global sufficient harvesting formula guarantees nonlinear predator extinction from arbitrary positive initial states and all finite gestation delays, meaningfully distinguishing local invasion resistance from global management intervention. These distinctions are not a mere parameter renaming or an unmotivated numerical slice. The positive-cone balance further shows that the local Hopf mechanism indicated in the source does not yield a biologically feasible small-amplitude periodic predator population, an interpretative distinction beyond linear stability. The scope explicitly addresses the ratio-dependent boundary singularity instead of assuming that every nonnegative history defines a classical solution.
